title: Your Support Team Should Ship Code – Lisa Orr, Zapier
talk_summary: Zapier built 'Scout', an agent that takes support tickets, categorizes them, assesses fixability, and generates merge requests via a plan/execute/validate CI pipeline, with support staff reviewing and iterating in GitLab. Key wins came from embedding tools into existing workflows (Zapier Zaps, MCP in Cursor) and owning orchestration rather than shipping a suite of standalone APIs.

takeaways.technique: Own the orchestration, don't ship a tool suite
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of exposing many standalone APIs for humans to pick from, they combined diagnosis + codegen into a single agent that runs the whole flow end-to-end.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what if we owned orchestration of these tools rather than saying here's a suite of tools you use them as you wish

takeaways.technique: Embed tools in the existing workflow surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Their APIs got little use as a separate web playground; adoption came when embedded into Zaps and MCP tools inside Cursor so users never left their working window.
takeaways.evidence_quote: So embedding tools is the key to usage as we find out.

takeaways.what_they_do: The codegen runs as a GitLab CI pipeline with three explicit phases — plan, execute, validate — before producing the MR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we run three phases in that pipeline. plan, execute and validate to generate this merge request

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure the agent on three concrete questions: was categorization right, was it actually fixable, was the code fix accurate; feedback becomes test cases over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we ask three questions categorization right is was it actually fixable uh and was the code fix accurate

takeaways.technique: Pre-qualify and pre-attach work to the queue
takeaways.what_they_do: Scout categorizes and assesses fixability before generating an MR, so only viable tickets enter the flow and the MR is already attached when a human picks it up.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Scout puts potentially fixable tickets right there in the triage flow. takes away a lot of the friction of looking for something to grab from the backlog.
takeaways.numbers: 40% of support team's app fixes generated by Scout; some doubled velocity from 1-2 to 3-4 tickets/week

takeaways.what_they_do: A diagnosis API gathers third-party API docs, logs, and external info and curates it into a diagnosis before codegen runs; this was the single most-valued tool.
